mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in the month preceding the decision date predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to market anticipation of rate hikes.
failure_condition: Over a 5-year rolling window, 20-day forward returns do not underperform the CPIAUCSL-based signal (t-test p > 0.05) during inflation spikes.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeding 135,000 in the prior month is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of sustained wage growth.
failure_condition: Across regimes with stable macro conditions, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to the PAYEMS signal (Rank IC < 0.05, two-tailed).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 (real GDP momentum) of at least 5% in the two months prior to the decision date predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals weakening aggregate demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < -5% change over two prior months
failure_condition: In contractionary regimes, the signal's predictive power is weak (p-value > 0.1 for out-of-sample tests).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO falling > 2% month-over-month in the prior month) combined with a decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates supply-side weakness, leading to a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate a rebound.
failure_condition: The interaction signal fails to predict positive 20-day returns in at least 60% of supply shocks (measured by NBER recession dates).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.2 percentage points in a single month, the 60-day S&P 500 forward return is expected to be negative as markets anticipate higher borrowing costs eroding equity valuations.
failure_condition: During non-tightening regimes, the FEDFUNDS rise does not produce a statistically significant negative 60-day forward return (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 5% for three consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as low labor-cost expectations support corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: The UNRATE signal is not predictive in high-inflation regimes (p-value > 0.05 in such regimes).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both RSAFS (retail sales momentum) and HOUST (housing starts) by at least 10% in the prior month indicate weakening demand across sectors, resulting in a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: During periods of excess supply, the combined signal fails to predict negative 5-day returns (empirical power < 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift from contraction to expansion as measured by a rising INDPRO trend (5 consecutive monthly increases of at least 1%) predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate supply normalization.
failure_condition: In periods of persistent over-supply (e.g., NBER recession), the INDPRO trend-up signal does not yield a statistically significant positive 20-day return (p > 0.1).
